transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making time for this calibration session. As you know, Taylor's annual performance review is due, and the current draft flags some missed deliverables as a concern. Before I finalize the rating and written review record, I want to make sure I have a complete picture. I'd like to go around and hear input from each of you — the project lead, a peer colleague, and HR — so we can factor in any context around the shifted priorities during this review cycle. Let's start with the project lead's perspective.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important before we go further. My project records show that exactly six of Taylor's delayed deliverables were delayed because leadership reprioritized the work after Taylor had already started it. I haven't yet added this attribution to the calibration notes, but it's directly relevant to the missed deliverables concern flagged in the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have something relevant to add from my perspective as a peer colleague. I directly observed exactly four occasions when Taylor identified a delivery risk early enough for the team to avoid an escalation. These examples haven't been collected in Taylor's review packet, but they demonstrate a pattern of proactive risk management that seems important for the calibration discussion.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share something from my side as HR. My confidential HR record confirms that Taylor worked under an approved 80 percent schedule for two months of the review cycle. This means the goals for that period must be recalibrated to 80 percent of the standard capacity. The record hasn't been shared previously because the schedule arrangement is confidential, but it's directly relevant to assessing the missed deliverables concern in the draft review.
